newsitem.title: ITALY: ALPINE SKIING-TOMBA GEARS UP FOR DRAMATIC FINALE.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-TOMBA GEARS UP FOR DRAMATIC FINALE.

text.p: Alberto Tomba has been dropping hints about a future career as a film actor, but his loyal Italian fans are demanding one last dazzling performance on the slopes before the curtain falls on the Alpine skiing world championships this weekend.

While the three times Olympic champion was in typically flamboyant form during an evening piste inspection -- "I'm ready for the movies," he told his audience -- there was an air of seriousness surrounding the floodlit dress rehearsal as Tomba prepared for the defence of his slalom title on Saturday.

Some have speculated it could be the last race of his remarkable career and if Tomba, winner of 48 World Cup races, is to forsake the hills for Hollywood, he will not want to be remembered for sliding out in failure as happened in Wednesday's giant slalom when he pulled up in the first leg.
He has already promised that "Saturday will be my day" and his supporters are desperate to see that prediction come true.

His boisterous fan club lined the course on Friday, chanting "Grande Alberto" (Great Alberto) and cheering the charismatic Italian's every move before cascading down the Kandahar piste behind their hero as he went to meet the media.

Police and paramilitary Carabinieri officers struggled to maintain some semblance of order as the crowd of reporters were swelled by toddlers and women in fur coats, plus any other bystander who happened to be in the area.
Tomba's fan club is expected to be joined by thousands more who will make the trek up from Turin and cities where ice is usually flavoured and sold in little tubs with a spoon.
Such is 'la Bomba's' popularity, television ratings are expected to rival the 13 million who tuned in for Wednesday's World Cup international between England and Italy at Wembley.
